instruction.text: Clara is talking with her teacher about a situation that happened on a social media app. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Someone posted a really embarrassing picture of me. Everyone can see it!
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '+1st'>Someone posted a really embarrassing picture of me. Everyone can see it!</prosody>

atoms.b: I’m sorry to hear that. That is absolutely not okay. It’s good that you’ve come to me about it. We can absolutely ((++resolve repeat)) this.
But what can we even do? The picture is already ((++online offline)).
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '+1st'>But what can we even do? The picture is already online.</prosody>

atoms.b: We can get the picture ((++deleted printed)). We’ll also make sure to talk with the person who posted it, so they know that something like this isn’t okay and is ((++unfair fair)).

instruction.text: Answer the questions about the conversation.

atoms.a: Who did Clara ask for help?
Which two things should Clara do now?
b: ++talk with the person who posted the picture

instruction.text: Luke is telling his dad about the comments on a picture he posted. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Someone wrote a mean comment on my picture. What should I do now? Everyone can read that.
I understand that it’s hurting you and making you worry. We can try to figure out who wrote the ((++comment book)). Do you have any idea?
I have no idea who it was. The person only has a ((++username full_name)).
Then we can ((++block like)) the person for now. This way, they can’t comment on your posts anymore. It’s also best to ((++not always)) reply to the comment.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the question.

hint.text: Anonymous means that a person’s identity is completely unknown, including their name.

atoms.text: If these examples were to continue happening, this would be cyberbullying. Cyberbullying is when people repeatedly upset, threaten or insult others on the internet. This often happens anonymously.
